title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Experimental Topics
description: Selected topics.

title: Special Study
description: Individual study.

title: Games, Play, and Learning
description: Analysis of games and play from cognitive, historical, motivational, and social perspectives. Design of simple learning games. Survey of the game industry and use of games in education and training.

title: Consciousness Hacking
description: Personal investigation into conscious awareness, identity, and mind. Exploration of mindfulness, self-inquiry, and similar contemporary approaches to personal awakening. Opportunities for direct experience with meditation, yoga, and related methods for expanding awareness, quieting mind, and cultivating communication, creativity, and intelligence.

title: Virtual Reality, Imaginary Worlds, and Future of Learning
description: Learning experiences using virtual reality and worlds. Cognitive load in novel environments, sensory perception, theories and models of social interaction. Implications of virtual interaction.

title: Educational Technology
description: Rationale, foundations, theories, careers, trends, and issues in educational technology. Implications of educational technology for instruction and information in schools, government, and corporations.

title: Instructional Design
description: Systematic design of products for education and training. Use of analyses and content mapping to set instructional goals. Instructional methods derived from learning theories for use in schools, universities, corporations, and other settings. Rapid prototyping of instructional products.

title: Advanced Multimedia Design for Learning
description: Educational visualization with digital video, animation, sound, 2D and 3D graphics for mobile and web-based learning.

title: Active Learning Strategies with Technology
description: Use of technology to support designing and managing instructor-led courses. Topics include building interactive activities, creating flipped videos and screencasts, developing online instruction that supports learners using Universal Design for Learning strategies, and harnessing the power of a learning management system.

title: Topics in Learning Design and Technology
description: Selected problems in educational technology.

title: Mobile Applications for Learning
description: Mobile learning models and examples. Design principles and development processes. Adapting mobile learning for different environments, settings, and cultures. Future trends.

title: Psychology of Technology-Based Learning
description: Principles of human learning and cognition applied to design and use of technology-based learning systems. Development of research-based guidelines for designing educational products and services.

title: Learning Through Games and Simulations
description: Design, evaluation, and use of simulations and games for education and training. Instructional applications of role plays, board games, and multiplayer virtual worlds. Theories of motivation and interest.

title: Learning Environment Design
description: Design and development of individualized instruction delivered through e-learning; learning management systems; informal learning for corporate and museum education.

title: Managing the Learning Design Process
description: Management of instructional design and performance interventions. Development of timelines, staffing plans, communication strategies, and budgets.

title: Performance Technology for Organizations
description: Organizational and informational systems that support instructional products and services. Individual, team, and organizational analyses. Incentives, feedback, coaching, job-aids, selection, knowledge management, and other performance improvement strategies.

title: Research Methods for Learning Design
description: Planning and executing research in learning design. Analyzing, interpreting, and reporting results to stakeholders.

title: Advanced Topics in Learning Design and Technology
description: Intensive study in specific areas of learning design and technology.

title: Seminar in Learning Design and Technology
description: Selected areas, topics in educational technology.

title: Directed Internship in Learning Design and Technology
description: Supervised internship in an educational or training setting. Application to take course must be made during preceding semester.

title: Advanced Seminar: Capstone Project
description: An intensive study culminating in a written project for a community-service-based learning client. Limited to students following Plan B for the Master of Arts degree.

title: Special Study
description: May involve fieldwork.

title: Thesis or Project
description: Preparation of a project or thesis for the master’s degree.

title: Thesis or Project Extension
description: Registration required in any semester or term following assignment of RP in Course 799A in which the student expects to use the facilities and resources of the university; also student must be registered in the course when the completed thesis or project is granted final approval.
